title: Inject the sender and formatter a service composes

blocks.text: Composition makes a service testable: it receives its parts through the constructor, so a test can hand it an in-memory sender that records what was sent. The page's design:
Both interfaces are given. Write `TemplateFormatter` and `NotificationService` in `Notifications`:

items: `TemplateFormatter.format` replaces **every** `${key}` with its value, and leaves a placeholder with no value as it is: `"Hi ${name}, bye ${name}! ${missing}"` with `name = Ann` is `"Hi Ann, bye Ann! ${missing}"`. A key is whatever lies between `${` and `}` (so `${user.name}` works), and a value is inserted exactly as it is: `$5` stays `$5`, and a value that looks like a placeholder, such as `${b}`, is not expanded again;

`new NotificationService(sender, formatter)` keeps **the parts it is given**, and `notify(recipient, template, variables)` formats with that formatter and sends with that sender. With a recording sender, `notify("admin", "Alert: ${event}", {event=login})` sends `"Alert: login"` to `admin` and returns `true`;

`notify` returns what the sender returned, and counts it: `getSuccessCount()` counts sends that returned `true`, `getFailureCount()` those that returned `false`. The page keeps both counts in `AtomicInteger`s so concurrent calls can share the service; the tests here check the counts one call at a time, and do not grade that choice.

cases.says: notify("admin", "Alert: ${event}", {event=login}) sends "Alert: login" and counts one success.
A send that returns false makes notify return false and is counted as a failure.
A service given an upper-casing formatter sends the upper-cased template: it uses the injected formatter.
Every placeholder is replaced, unknown ones stay, keys may hold a dot, and values ($5, ${b}) are inserted as they are.

concepts: Dependencies injected through the constructor can be replaced by test doubles, so each composed part is tested in isolation.
A template formatter replaces every ${key} placeholder with its value.
